TIP 1: Personal expenses on corporate card by CFO of Heronforge Industrial
CHANNEL: encrypted email
RECEIVED: 02 May 2026

I am writing about Andriy Kovalenko, the Chief Financial Officer of Heronforge Industrial, a publicly traded mid-cap industrial manufacturer headquartered in Cleveland (NYSE: HFI). I have been Mr. Kovalenko's executive assistant since June 2022. I am submitting this anonymously through a personal email account.

I am reporting a sustained pattern of personal expenses being charged to Mr. Kovalenko's corporate American Express card and reimbursed by Heronforge as legitimate business expenses. The pattern has been consistent for the entire period I have been in the role, and I have been instructed by Mr. Kovalenko on multiple specific occasions to code the charges in ways that would not draw attention from the corporate accounting team.

I want to provide specific evidence rather than impressions. The following are six representative transactions I have personally processed, each of which I can produce supporting documents for:

1. 14 March 2024 — $11,840 — booked through Heronforge's corporate travel agency to "Aerial Concierge" for a chartered flight from Cleveland Burke Lakefront to Eagle County Regional Airport (Vail, CO). Trip dates 14-21 March 2024, returning 21 March. Mr. Kovalenko's wife Daria Kovalenko and their two children, Pavel (age 14) and Mira (age 11), traveled with him. The trip was coded in our expense system as "executive recruiting - Western region." Heronforge has no recruiting operations or open executive searches in Colorado.

2. 22 May 2024 — $4,260 — Aspen Mountain Lodge, folio number AML-24-05227, four nights, two rooms. Coded as "industry conference travel." There was no industry conference in Aspen during those dates that Heronforge sponsored, attended, or for which Mr. Kovalenko was a registered attendee.

3. 11 August 2024 — $9,720 — Bayside Yacht Charter, Lake Erie, full-day private charter for twelve passengers. Coded as "client entertainment - regional banking." The guest list, which I assembled for Mr. Kovalenko, consisted of his immediate family, his sister-in-law and her husband, and three friends from his country club. No Heronforge clients or counterparties were on the guest list.

4. 27 December 2024 — $3,180 — Cardinal Sound Audio of Cleveland, invoice 25-CSA-882, installation of a home theater system. The invoice address is Mr. Kovalenko's residence on Lakeshore Boulevard. Coded as "office equipment and installation."

5. 18-25 February 2025 — $14,330 — Four Seasons Resort Maui, folio FSM-25-118843, suite booking for seven nights. Coded as "investor conference - West Coast." Heronforge held no investor events in Hawaii during this period. The Q1 2025 investor day was held virtually on 12 February.

6. 04 April 2025 — $7,290 — Belmont Diamonds of Cleveland, invoice BD-25-0184, described on the invoice as "anniversary purchase." Coded as "executive gifts - retention."

The total of items I can specifically document is approximately $51,000 across the period. I believe the overall pattern is materially larger; these are the six transactions where I personally retained the underlying receipts, folios, or invoices. I have these on a personal device.

I have also retained:

- The expense reports as submitted, with my coding notes.
- A March 2024 email from Mr. Kovalenko instructing me to "use the recruiting code, talk to me before submitting if there's any question."
- The travel agency itinerary records showing the family-member passengers.
- The Amex statements showing the underlying card charges (within my legitimate access as his EA).

I am prepared to provide all of this to an investigator under written confidentiality.

TIP 2: Heronforge CFO using company money for personal stuff
CHANNEL: intake form
RECEIVED: 04 May 2026

I used to work at Heronforge a few years ago. I'm not going to name where I worked specifically because I don't want this traced back to me. But I wanted to write in because I keep hearing things about the CFO and the way he uses company money and I think someone should look into it.

The CFO's name is Andriy Kovalenko. He has been there for several years and basically runs the place financially. From what people have told me he uses the corporate card for all kinds of personal stuff. I've heard from a friend who is still in finance there that he flies his family on the company dime, takes vacations and calls them business trips, that kind of thing. Apparently it's been going on for a long time and everyone in finance kind of knows.

His wife is always around at company events and she goes on a lot of the trips. People joke about it. There was something about a vacation in Aspen or Vail or somewhere that was supposedly a business trip but everyone knew it wasn't. And I heard he bought himself something pretty expensive for his anniversary and put it on the company.

I don't have documents. I haven't worked there in a couple years and I never had access to the expense system anyway. But I'm pretty sure if you talked to people in the finance department they would tell you the same thing. There's also rumors that the audit committee knows and hasn't done anything because the CEO and the CFO are close personal friends.

The reason I'm writing now is because the company just announced they're going to do a stock buyback and I think investors should know that the CFO has been treating the company like his personal piggybank while they're spending shareholder money. It's not right.

I would talk to a reporter but I would need to be sure I couldn't be identified. I don't have specific dates or amounts but I can tell you this is real and someone should look into it.
